meta.documentDescription: Portfolio of Andres Enrique Ortiz Santa Cruz, backend-oriented Full-Stack developer in Île-de-France.

home.intro: I am a Mexican Full-Stack developer based in Paris. I have done different projects using a variety of technologies and tools.

snippet.comment: Currently a backend apprentice at Aphilia.

about.bio1: Hello, I'm Andres Enrique Ortiz Santa Cruz, a *Backend-oriented Full-Stack developer*.
about.bio2: I design and build web applications and services with *TypeScript, Node.js and React*, with a particular interest in *software architecture, distributed systems, AI and cybersecurity*.

aphilia.task1: Feature work across the stack, mostly back-end (NestJS, TypeORM, MySQL): menu and item management — catalogues, prices, promotions — plus new React components on the front end.
aphilia.task2: AI integration: design and integration of conversational agents and intelligent assistants — skill definition, rules engine and specialised prompts.
aphilia.task3: Cut p50 latency on the listing endpoints by 18%, by replacing to-many joins with a single batch query.
aphilia.task4: Diagnosed 50-second lock waits and HTTP 429 errors with Datadog, then cleared them by optimising the SQL behind them.
aphilia.task5: Built Datadog dashboards (application health, API latency, sync success/failure) and added structured logs, so terminal sync problems can be traced.
aphilia.task6: Wrote the Jest (unit and integration) and Cypress (end-to-end) suites that run in CI, and ran load tests.
aphilia.task7: Used Claude Code daily, reviewing and validating every generated change before merging.

jobtracker.task1: Monorepo on pnpm workspaces and Turborepo: a Next.js 16 web app, a NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL API, and Zod contracts shared by both ends.
jobtracker.task2: Email classified by prioritised rules in three languages, with an optional AI second opinion (Claude Haiku 4.5 or a local Ollama) called only when the rules are unsure, and capped by a monthly budget.
jobtracker.task3: Incremental Gmail sync over the History API with a search fallback, resumable in chunks and driven by a cron. An application's status is recomputed by replaying its events, so the order the email arrives in does not matter.
jobtracker.task4: Privacy by design: message bodies are never stored, what the AI sees is redacted of addresses and phone numbers, and Settings deletes the account and everything attached to it.
jobtracker.task5: Hardening: per-request nonce CSP, helmet, rate limits, Zod on every input, Vitest + Testcontainers + Playwright in CI, and a deploy that fits in the free tiers of Vercel, Render and Neon.

meta.documentDescription: Portfolio of Andres Enrique Ortiz Santa Cruz, junior application security consultant / DevSecOps in Île-de-France.

home.intro: I am a Mexican developer based in Paris, moving from backend into application security. I work with development teams to find, prioritise and fix vulnerabilities.

snippet.comment: Developer by background, moving into application security.

about.bio1: Hello, I'm Andres Enrique Ortiz Santa Cruz, a *developer moving into application security*.
about.bio2: I build with *TypeScript, Node.js and NestJS*, and I bring that to security teams as an *enabler*: my goal is to identify, prioritise and help development teams fix vulnerabilities — not to hand them a report and walk away.

aphilia.task1: Wrote the Jest and Cypress (end-to-end) suites that run in CI, with lint on every pull request, and ran load tests.
aphilia.task2: Reviewed and validated all the code generated by an AI assistant (Claude Code) before it was merged.
aphilia.task3: Diagnosed 50-second lock waits and HTTP 429 errors with Datadog, then cleared them by optimising the SQL behind them.
aphilia.task4: Built Datadog dashboards (application health, errors, API latency) and added structured logs to trace incidents.
aphilia.task5: Developed back-end features (NestJS, TypeORM, MySQL) and React components, and fixed bugs.

jobtracker.task1: Applied data minimisation: email bodies are never stored, and a user can delete their account and every record attached to it.
jobtracker.task2: Limited the data-leak surface of the LLM: personal data is redacted before any call, the AI is only ever a second opinion, and spend is capped by a monthly budget.
jobtracker.task3: Hardened the app: per-request nonce CSP, security headers through helmet, rate limiting, and Zod validation on every input.
jobtracker.task4: Automated the tests in CI with Vitest, Testcontainers and Playwright, plus a dependency audit that fails the build on a high vulnerability.
jobtracker.task5: Built on a pnpm/Turborepo monorepo: Next.js 16 web app, NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL API, Zod contracts shared by both ends.
